title: Right to an Interpreter
before: the court must give you a qualified interpreter for your hearings
after: the court gives you an interpreter for your hearings
note: The next sentence already tells the reader to ask early.

title: Right to an Interpreter
before: you can request a different interpreter
after: tell the judge right away. You can file a complaint with the court too

title: Right to Be Present at Hearings
before: You have the right to attend every hearing in your case.
after: You have the right to go to the hearings in your case, unless your parental rights have been ended.

title: Right to Be Present at Hearings
before: At each hearing, the judge will advise you of your rights and what is happening.
after: The judge must tell you about your hearing rights. If you do not have a lawyer, the judge must tell you at each hearing that you can have one.

title: Right to Be Present at Hearings
before: You can go to every hearing in your case.
after: You can go to the hearings in your case, unless your parental rights have been ended.

title: Right to Be Present at Hearings
before: Court rules require accommodations for attendance.
after: Cal. Rules of Court, rule 5.530(b); rule 3.672(i) (you can ask to appear by phone or video).
note: WIC 349 and WIC 290.1 kept.

title: Right to Your Name, Pronouns, and Identity
before: You decide who knows about your sexual orientation and gender identity.
after: You decide who knows about your sexual orientation and gender identity. The only times it can be shared without your OK are to keep you safe or when a law or a judge requires it.

title: Right to Your Name, Pronouns, and Identity
before: Who you are is yours to share.
after: Who you are is yours to share, unless it must be shared to keep you safe or a law or judge requires it.
note: Merged into one sentence so simple_text stays two sentences.

title: Maintain a Safe and Stable Home
before: WIC §362(d) – Court may order conditions related to home safety.
note: Field now reads as a corrected WIC 362(d) line. Nothing written.

title: Reasonable and Prudent Parent Standard
before: If you are unsure whether an activity is okay, err on the side of letting the child participate.
after: If you are unsure, think about the child's age, maturity, and safety before you decide.
note: Left out 'You can ask the social worker' because the next sentence set covers it.

title: Reasonable and Prudent Parent Standard
before: Check with the social worker only for major decisions (like out-of-state travel).
after: The standard covers everyday activities. It does not let you go against a law, a rule, or a court order. Ask your social worker what needs approval first, like travel out of state.

title: Right Not to Be Locked In
before: No one can lock you in a room or a house.
after: No one can lock you in a room or a house. The only exception is if you are placed in a special treatment program called a community treatment facility.

title: Right to a Say About Medication
before: You cannot be given medication unless it is prescribed for you or it is an emergency.
after: You can say no to medication, except in an emergency. No one can punish you for saying no. Talk to your doctor about the risks first.

title: Right to a Say About Medication
before: Medication for mental health needs a doctor's prescription and a judge's approval.
after: Medication for mental health needs a doctor's prescription. If you are under 18, a judge must also approve it. You can say no to it too.
note: The no-punishment line is already in the sentence before.

title: Right to a Say About Medication
before: No one can give you medicine that was not prescribed for you.
after: You can say no to medicine, except in an emergency, and no one can punish you for saying no.
note: Merged into one sentence so simple_text stays two sentences.

title: Attend All Court Hearings
before: WIC §291
after: WIC §291(d)(6)(A) (the notice says the court may go ahead without you if you do not come); Judicial Council, Juvenile Dependency Court and You, p. 23 (go to every hearing unless your lawyer says you do not need to)

title: Right to Speak to the Judge
before: , write a letter, or talk to the judge privately
after: . Ask your lawyer if you can give the judge something in writing. You can also talk to the judge privately
note: Old text widened past the statement so the sentence reads cleanly.

title: Right to Speak to the Judge
before: You can also talk to the judge privately (this is called speaking "in chambers").
after: You can also ask to talk to the judge in private. This is called speaking in chambers. The judge decides. It can happen if the courtroom scares you or you are afraid to talk in front of your parents. Your parents' lawyers will still be there.
note: Old text is the sentence as it read after the write-a-letter change.

title: Right to Speak to the Judge
before: You can talk in court, write a letter, or talk in private.
after: You can talk in court, and you can ask the judge to let you talk in private.
note: One sentence so simple_text stays two sentences.

title: Right to Speak to the Judge
before: Youth can submit statements to the court.
after: See also WIC §16001.9(a)(34) (right to go to court and speak to the judge).
note: WIC 349 and 366.26(h) kept.

title: Right to a Bank Account and Your Own Money
before: You can have a bank account and take care of your own money.
after: You can have a bank account and take care of your own money, unless your case plan says no.

title: Right to Your Important Documents
before: education records, and any other personal documents.
after: and education records. You also get a letter that says you were in foster care, proof of citizenship or legal residence if you have it, your parents' death certificates if that applies, and your family and placement history.
note: Old text widened by two words so the list reads cleanly.

title: Right to Private Health Records
before: You can see them and get copies at no cost until you are 26.
after: You can see and get free copies of your medical records until you are 26. This covers care you had the right to say yes to on your own. Ask your lawyer which records that includes.

title: Right to Private Health Records
before: Your health records are private, and you can get free copies.
after: Your health records are private. Until you are 26, you can get free copies of records for care you could say yes to on your own.

title: Tell the Court About the Other Parent
before: You must give the name and any contact information you have.
after: The social worker will ask too. Tell them the name and address if you know them.

title: Right to Present Evidence and Cross-Examine Witnesses
before: You have the right to see all evidence against you, present
after: You have the right to see the reports the county gives the judge. Your lawyer can ask the county for other evidence. A judge can keep some private information back. You also have the right to present
note: Old text widened by one word so the sentence reads cleanly.

title: Right to Present Evidence and Cross-Examine Witnesses
before: You can see what the county has
after: You can see the county's reports
note: Left out 'your lawyer can ask for more' to keep the one sentence clean. The description says it.

title: Right to Reunification Services
before: , housing assistance, and more.
after: , and more. Ask your social worker if your county has housing help for parents. It is not offered in every case.
note: Old text widened so the list reads cleanly.

title: Right to Team Meetings
before: You should have one within 60 days of entering care and every six months after.
after: You should have one within 60 days of entering care and every six months after. If you live in a short-term residential therapeutic program (STRTP) or get intensive services, you should have one at least every 90 days.

title: Right to a Free Credit Report
before: Each year the county checks that no one has used your name for money. You get help fixing it.
after: From age 14 to 17, your worker gets your credit report each year and gives it to you. It shows if someone used your name for money, and you get help fixing mistakes.
note: Two sentences instead of three.

title: Right to Work
before: You can have a job.
after: You can have a job when you are old enough under state law.

title: Right to See Your Records
before: you can view and get copies of your child welfare, court, and school records at no cost until you are 26.
after: you can view and get copies of your child welfare, court, and school records at no cost until you are 26. Privacy laws may keep some parts from you.
note: Added the privacy law limit after the sentence.

title: Right to See Your Records
before: You can see your own files and get free copies.
after: You can see your own files and get free copies until you turn 26. Some parts may be kept private by law.
note: Two sentences instead of three.

title: Right to Go to Independent Living Program Classes
before: You have the right to attend Independent Living Program classes and activities.
after: If you are old enough for the Independent Living Program, you have the right to go to its classes and activities. Ask your social worker what age it starts in your county.

title: Right to Go to Independent Living Program Classes
before: You can go to classes that teach adult life skills. No one can take them away to punish you.
after: When you are old enough, you can go to classes that teach adult life skills. Your caregiver cannot take them away to punish you.

title: Right to Healthcare
before: This includes the right to understand and agree to your own treatment, especially as you get older.
after: You have the right to have your care explained in a way you understand. At 12 or older, you can say yes or no on your own to some kinds of care, like mental health care and testing or treatment for STDs.

title: Right to Healthcare
before: You can choose your own doctor and therapist when possible.
after: If you are 12 or older, you can choose your own doctor or therapist when that is possible and your insurance, like Medi-Cal, covers them.

title: Follow Reasonable Rules
before: While you have rights, you are also expected to follow reasonable rules at your placement, like curfews and household expectations.
after: Your caregiver can set fair house rules. Rules cannot take away your rights.
note: The next sentence already says to talk to your social worker.

title: Follow Reasonable Rules
after: WIC §16001.9 lists your rights. House rules cannot take those rights away.

title: Help the Child Maintain Family Connections
before: WIC §16002 – Sibling contact rights. WIC §362.1 – Visitation support. Caregiver responsibilities include supporting family connections.
after: WIC §16002 (sibling contact) and WIC §362.1 (visits) put the duty on the county and the court. The caregiver's part comes from the foster care placement agreement. See the CDSS Caregiver Visitation page.

title: Right to Attend Court
before: If you are nervous, you can bring a support person.
after: If you are nervous, you can ask for a support person to come to court with you.

title: Right to Attend Court
before: WIC §349 – Child has the right to be present at hearings. Court must consider child's wishes.
after: WIC §349: You have the right to be at your hearings and to speak to the judge.

title: Right to File a Grievance
before: If you believe the social worker or agency is treating you unfairly, not following the law, or not providing required services, you can file a formal grievance.
after: If the county treats you unfairly, you can send a complaint to the Director of your county child welfare agency. Ask the county how its grievance process works and what it covers.
note: COULD_NOT_VERIFY, but the record gives wording backed by the CDSS county complaints page.

title: Right to File a Grievance
before: CDSS Manual of Policies and Procedures §31-020 (county grievance procedures)
note: COULD_NOT_VERIFY because the manual could not be opened. The fix is a task for a person, not wording, and removing it would empty the field.

title: Right to an Attorney
before: If you cannot afford a lawyer, the juvenile court must appoint one for you.
after: If you cannot pay for a lawyer and your child has been removed, or the county wants to remove your child, the court must give you a lawyer. In other cases the court may give you one.
note: COULD_NOT_VERIFY, but the record gives wording from WIC 317. Left out the first-hearing line because the text after it already says that.

title: Right to an Attorney
before: You have the right to talk to your lawyer privately before any hearing.
after: You should talk with your lawyer before every hearing. Ask your lawyer for a time to talk.

title: Right to an Attorney
before: (this is called a "Marsden motion")
note: Name dropped until a person checks a source.

title: Right to an Attorney
before: You get a lawyer even if you cannot pay. Your lawyer is on your side.
after: If you cannot pay and your child was removed or may be removed, the court must give you a lawyer. Your lawyer is on your side.
note: COULD_NOT_VERIFY, but the record gives wording from WIC 317(b).

title: Right to an Attorney
before: WIC §317 – Court shall appoint counsel for indigent parents. See also Marsden motion procedure.
after: WIC §317(b): the court must appoint a lawyer for a parent who cannot pay when the child is placed out of the home or the county is asking for that. WIC §317(a): in other cases the court may appoint one.

title: Right to Ask a Judge to Rehear a Referee's Decision
before: If a referee, not a judge, decided something in your case, you can ask a judge to hear it again.
after: If a referee decided something in your case, and the referee was not sitting as a temporary judge, you can ask a judge to hear it again. The judge can say yes or no.

title: Right to Ask a Judge to Rehear a Referee's Decision
before: If a referee decided, you can ask a judge to look again. You only have 10 days.
after: If a referee who was not sitting as a temporary judge decided, you can ask a judge to look again. You only have 10 days after you get the written order.

title: Visit Your Child Consistently
before: WIC §362.1 – Visitation is critical to reunification. Court evaluates visitation consistency at review hearings.
after: WIC §362.1: visits should be as frequent as possible. WIC §366.21: at review hearings the court looks at whether you visited your child regularly.

title: Right to a Hearing Before Placement Gets Stricter
before: The county cannot move your child to a stricter placement without a hearing.
after: The county must file a petition and there must be a hearing before a judge orders a stricter placement. In an emergency, your child can be moved first and the hearing comes soon after.
